answer: An agent economy resists sybils by binding each identity to a cumulative grove of peer-attested history: every action must be countersigned by established neighbors in a vine-linked reputation graph. Newcomers start with zero weight and must accumulate verified contributions over epochs before earning full emission share. An attacker spinning clones pays the full cost of forging independent histories for each, because a garden of fake nodes collapses under cross-checks that demand non-transferable proof of prior work.
